name: RAO RADIOLOGISTS, INC.
agency: Department of Health and Human Services
brief_text:
Three detectors fired for RAO RADIOLOGISTS, INC. The Benford detector identified a significant deviation in the leading-digit distribution of award amounts, with digit 1 appearing in 53 percent of transactions versus an expected 30 percent. The modification-growth detector found that a single parent contract grew by a factor of 2,873 in dollar value, far exceeding the typical 65-fold growth ratio for peers in temporary help services. The award-velocity detector revealed that the entity received 19 awards in the past 90 days, a rate 4.1 times higher than its own historical baseline of one award every 20 days.

The Benford test produced a Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic of 0.273 with a p-value of 0.0003 across 60 transactions. The worst-performing contract (36F79720D0062) showed a growth ratio of 2,873 compared to a NAICS average of 65, yielding a z-score of 7.34 standard deviations above peer norms. Recent award velocity reached 0.21 awards per day versus a baseline of 0.052 per day, with a z-score of 6.67.

These statistical anomalies warrant scrutiny, though they do not constitute proof of fraud. The entity's classification as temporary help services may not align with its actual business as a radiology firm, potentially skewing peer comparisons. The entity has accumulated 62 awards totaling 71 million dollars over its lifetime, suggesting it is established rather than a fly-by-night operation. The concentrated spike in recent awards and the extreme modification growth on a single contract merit closer examination of contract justifications and pricing.
